status: Author development proposals, not additional user requirements. Apply before any scene becomes accepted canon.
recurring_details: Meles is Thestor's nephew and apprentice. Grain and passage are paid through obligations and a notched tally, not minted coins or modern vouchers. A stolen sacred bronze basin in Agamemnon's camp creates a concrete unresolved debt. No modern administrative or psychological language.

scenes.beats: Thestor finishes steering-oar fittings while a departing boat is being loaded; Meles has packed their small bundle. The storm has exposed a damaged sealed metal fragment, not a usable weapon. Thestor cleans enough to recognize a cult mark remembered from his father's workshop, then deliberately hides the mark under a cloth until his request for passage is refused. He chooses to reveal it as a last bargaining resource, risking confiscation. Odysseus recognizes the coastal cult from earlier voyages, giving a reason to investigate Cape Lekton rather than inexplicable geographic knowledge from a stamp. Thestor insists on grain for Meles before surrendering the fragment; Odysseus delivers grain but makes passage conditional on recovering the shrine's property. Thestor accepts a particular gain for the boy at the cost of his own immediate departure. End with the boat taking another passenger while Thestor retrieves his tools for the expedition. Keep one dawn-to-midday sequence; do not discover it today and claim several prior days of work.
scenes.change: Thestor knowingly exchanges the fragment and his labor for the boy's food and conditional passage; Odysseus commits a boat and crew. No functioning weapon or demonstration.

scenes.beats: Three days later a small crew lands below the coastal shrine. Give the journey and resistance real scene space: tide, unloading, and a difficult climb with the fragment must cost effort or equipment. The human keeper wants restoration of a particular sacred bronze basin looted years earlier and now used in Agamemnon's camp. Odysseus recognizes his own part in its removal. He cannot pledge the king's property publicly, and an offer of hypothetical Trojan spoil is refused. He leaves his personal seal as surety and undertakes to restore the basin within a moon; the missing seal and concealed obligation create political exposure. The keeper makes a single demonstration only after accepting the pledge. Twenty-five prepared charges are counted before that demonstration, one is consumed, and exactly twenty-four are physically transported out with six heavy single-shot tubes. Carrying and securing the cache must be enacted, not skipped. The tubes were entrusted to defend the harbor and are to be returned, not given as unlimited spoils. Do not reproduce construction or loading instructions.
scenes.change: Six weapons and twenty-four remaining charges return to camp after the keeper's single demonstration; Odysseus has surrendered his seal and secretly owes the sacred basin.

scenes.beats: The council and trial share one continuous setting beside the ships; never reconvene the same council. Agamemnon puts his token on the rack to claim custody. Achilles initially withholds his men because the weapon separates the wielder from the danger imposed on workers. One test charge is consumed: the shot splinters timber, burns Thestor's hand, and briefly blinds nearby men in smoke. A second prepared charge is discovered damp and set aside, still counted among the remaining supply; it is not fired or consumed here. Establish these vulnerabilities through action. Thestor withholds his good hand from the next demand until operators are assigned protection and Meles's passage is acknowledged. Achilles gives his own shield-men to the operators, a costly concession of manpower rather than conversion to enthusiasm. Agamemnon retains custody but must accept this condition. A visible Trojan movement makes the limited deployment consequential. End with assignments and material preparation, not a lecture on honor.
scenes.change: One test charge spent: twenty-three remain, including one suspect damp charge. Thestor has an injured hand. A specific bargain commits Achilles's men to protect operators while the king keeps ownership.

scenes.beats: Begin at the contested approach, with the cache already acquired and the council complete. Four charges are consumed in this scene: three shots and one failed damp charge, leaving nineteen. The first shot misses its intended primary target. A later casualty gets a brief concrete human particular, not an invented moral epitaph. Smoke hides the operators' vulnerability; the damp charge fails to fire; while the exposed frame is dragged to cover, its support sinks in rain-softened ground, the tube strikes stone and its collar breaks, trapping Meles. Do not imply damp powder itself causes a destructive discharge. Thestor's previously burned hand impedes rescue. Achilles gives up a real opportunity to pursue Hector so he can shield and extract the operators; the earlier protection bargain is now costly action. Thestor must abandon the damaged weapon to free the boy. Hector responds to observed smoke, pauses and disorder, disperses his men and withdraws in order; he cannot know ammunition counts or internal operation. Greeks hold the limited position. Meles has an irreversible injury with no instant cure. Five usable tubes and nineteen charges remain; the missing sixth tube and Odysseus's seal/basin obligation carry consequences into the larger story. End on a specific act of custody, care or owed restitution, without explaining the theme or announcing victory's significance.
scenes.change: Local ground held; Hector and Achilles survive. Five usable weapons, nineteen charges, a wounded apprentice, a lost damaged tube, and the still-unfulfilled sacred restitution remain.

cast_registry.thestor: Mortal Achaean smith and uncle/master of Meles; NOT a priest, seer, god, blind man or the sanctuary keeper. Travels with Odysseus.
cast_registry.meles: Thestor’s nephew and apprentice. Remains in the Ithacan camp during scene 2; NOT the keeper’s relative or guardian.
cast_registry.odysseus: Achaean king of Ithaca, bargaining expedition leader.
cast_registry.agamemnon: Achaean coalition commander and king of Mycenae.
cast_registry.achilles: Achaean warrior and Myrmidon leader, not a Trojan.
cast_registry.hector: Trojan prince and commander; has no private Greek inventory or bargain knowledge.
cast_registry.sanctuary_keeper: A distinct unnamed human priest of Hephaestus, guarding the shrine; NOT Thestor or a disguised member of the Greek party.
